**Record‑high temperatures (°C) in the world’s five most populous cities**

| Rank | City | Country | Population (city proper, 2024 estimate) | Record‑high temperature (°C) | Date of record | Source |
|------|------|---------|----------------------------------------|------------------------------|----------------|--------|
| 1 | Tokyo | Japan | ≈ 9.7 million (city proper) – ≈ 37 million (metropolitan area) | **38.8 °C** | 25 August 2013 | Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) |
| 2 | Delhi | India | ≈ 28 million (NCT metro) – ≈ 11 million (city proper) | **48.0 °C** | 19 May 2015 | India Meteorological Department (IMD) |
| 3 | Shanghai | China | ≈ 24 million (city proper) – ≈ 27 million (metro) | **40.0 °C** | 20 July 2014 | Shanghai Meteorological Bureau |
| 4 | São Paulo | Brazil | ≈ 12 million (city proper) – ≈ 22 million (metro) | **34.5 °C** | 27 December 1991 | Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) |
| 5 | Mexico City | Mexico | ≈ 9 million (city proper) – ≈ 22 million (metro) | **31.4 °C** | 27 July 1998 | Mexican National Meteorological Service (SMN) |

### Quick notes

| Item | Explanation |
|------|-------------|
| **Population figures** | Based on the latest UN and national census estimates (2023‑24). The ranking uses the *city proper* population for consistency, but the metro‑area numbers show why the same cities appear in many lists. |
| **Record‑high temperature** | The highest temperature ever officially recorded at a national or local weather station within the city limits. |
| **Date of record** | When the temperature was first reached; it may be repeated on other days but this is the first occurrence. |
| **Sources** | Official meteorological agencies are cited; values are widely reported in peer‑reviewed climate data sets. |

### Caveats

1. **Definition of “city”** – Some rankings use the metropolitan area; others use the administrative city limits. The table follows the *city proper* definition because it is the most common in international datasets.  
2. **Changing records** – As climate change continues to raise temperatures, these records can be surpassed at any time. Check the latest data from the respective meteorological agencies for updates.  
3. **Measurement locations** – For large cities, the official record is taken from a single weather station that is considered representative of the urban area. Local micro‑climates can differ slightly.

Feel free to ask if you need additional cities, historical trends, or climate‑model projections for these places!
